issues.problem: The CJK caption splitter cuts numbers, times and domains that sit inside a CJK word into two pops. It also pops punctuation on its own after an *accent* phrase or after an ASCII opening quote. This contradicts what the GUIDE and the code comment now promise: "punctuation stays with its character, a Latin word or a number stays whole" and "a run of Latin letters or digits stays one". The worker's report and commit 0febd80 say the a7 caption pops "布，", but the tokenizer actually gives 布|，.
issues.evidence: Node probe monitor/tok.mjs against wt-reel _reel.js: 提升3.5倍 → 提|升|3.|5|倍; 仅需9.9元 → 仅|需|9.|9|元; 1,000+用户 → 1,|000+|用|户; 下午3:30开始 → 下|午|3:|30|开|始; manus.im官网 → manus.|im|官|网; *新品*！ → 新|品|！; "新品"发布 → "|新|品"|发|布; 「新品」*发布*，iPhone… → 「新|品」|发|布|，|iPhone|…. The cause is in reelPieces: a \p{Po} character after a Latin/digit run is classed 't', and the next digit or letter (prev === 't') starts a new piece. A word that begins with tail punctuation (the next .lv-w span after an accent part) becomes a piece by itself. Rendered proof: monitor/jobs/r8, frames a1-0018/0022/0026 → monitor/frames/r8_pop_strip.png. "3." pops with the accent plate, then "5" pops alone about 0.2 s later. Prices, ratings and multipliers like these are very common in Chinese marketing captions. Node and Chrome still agree on the count: the mc storyboard renders in all 3 aspects with rc 0, so this is cosmetic.
issues.required_fix: In reelPieces, keep a Latin/number piece open across punctuation when a letter or digit follows. For example, track the current piece's base class and let a run character after a 't' join when that base is a Latin/digit run, so 3.5, 9.9, 1,000, 3:30 and manus.im stay whole. Treat an ASCII " or ' at the start of a word as an opening mark. For a span that starts with closing punctuation after an accent part, either merge that piece into the previous pop (in reelCapWords and in the browser split together, so the counts still match) or say in the GUIDE and the comment that punctuation right after an accent phrase pops on its own. Add these cases to the unit cases, and correct the 布， claim in the report.
